The San Francisco 49ers return home from their season-opening trip to Melbourne looking to build on a 1-0 start when they host the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. San Francisco is riding high after taking down the Los Angeles Rams , and the 49ers will look to continue to build on their early-season success against the lowly Dolphins.

It's about as lopsided a consensus as you'll find in Week 2 — we checked in with seven outlets' expert panels, and 50 of 52 total picks favor the 49ers. Only Bleacher Report's Brad Gagnon was brave enough to take the Dolphins in this matchup.

articles.title: Behind enemy lines: Previewing Rams-Giants with 5 key questions
articles.summary: Previewing Monday's Rams-Giants game with Dan Benton of Giants Wire, where he gives his take on this big matchup.
articles.body:
Following their season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers , the Los Angeles Rams will try to secure their first win of the season Monday night against the New York Giants . The Giants , however, look much better than anticipated, beating the Dallas Cowboys in Week 1, 28-20.

The Rams are back at home this week after a long trip to Australia, so they'll be in front of their fans at SoFi Stadium. The Giants, meanwhile, have to travel across the country for this matchup.

To preview Rams-Giants in Week 2, we asked Giants Wire lead writer Dan Benton five questions, including a prediction for how the game will go.

1. The Giants were incredibly efficient on offense against the Cowboys. Do you expect a similar performance against the Rams?

Giants Wire: I think it's important to remember that the Dallas defense was terrible in 2025 and really doesn't look much better after one week this season. That's not to be a Debbie Downer or dismiss the Giants' obvious offensive improvements, but reality always lies somewhere in the middle. They fumbled four times, and had they lost more than one, we'd all have a very different vision of that game in our heads. With all of that having been said, there is a reason for optimism in East Rutherford -- the offensive scheme was night and day compared to the Daboll era. From Greg Roman to Matt Nagy to John Harbaugh, you can see the many years of experience and success. Still, it's early in the season, and the identity of this offense is only just beginning to take shape. How that translates on Monday night? We'll see, but I wouldn't expect the same level of success or efficiency against a defense that, at least on paper, is better than Dallas'.

2. New York didn't sack Dak Prescott , but how did the pass rush perform as a whole in that win?

Giants Wire: Prescott was quick to deliver the ball, but much like Stafford against San Francisco , he was under consistent pressure. The Giants have enough talent to move players around and set up a NASCAR-like package with Kayvon Thibodeaux inside and both Brian Burns and Abdul Carter coming off the edges. Arvell Reese can also be moved around and generate pressure from inside or outside, which I expect to see a little more of as the season wears on. They may not have had any sacks of Prescott, but they certainly made him uncomfortable. Carter, specifically, has elite talent and athleticism, and has become almost impossible to block one-on-one.

3. Does Malik Nabers look like his usual self to you after coming back from his knee injury?

Giants Wire: He looked better than many expected, but he's certainly not 100 percent. Most players coming back from a torn ACL take a year to truly return to form, so I wouldn't expect to see rookie-like Nabers for a little bit of time. Still, he flashed some of the game-changing talent he became known for in 2024, and his presence alone helped create some mismatches elsewhere. There were a few slips and he admitted to being rusty, but even at 75 percent, he's better than most receivers in the NFL.

4. Who's an underrated Giants player for Rams fans to know?

Giants Wire: Does Patrick Ricard count as underrated? If he did, I would absolutely name him because he's very much a part of what the Giants do offensively. If we have to dig deeper, I would say tight end Chris Manhertz , who is not going to wow anyone with his pass-catching prowess (although he is consistent), but absolutely makes an impact in 12 and 22 personnel. He is an elite run blocker and plus pass protector, and with him leading the way, followed by the aforementioned Ricard and running back Cam Skattebo... Watch out.

5. Who wins on Monday night and what's the final score?

Giants Wire: I'm not ready to subscribe to the theory that the Giants will experience a miracle turnaround in Year 1 under John Harbaugh en route to the NFC East crown and playoffs. However, I am willing to entertain the idea that this latest "rebuild" may already be ahead of schedule. That will still come with hiccups, which I expect them to experience on Monday night in Los Angeles against a starving and angry Rams team that may have Aaron Donald back on the field. Add in the Giants' ailing secondary, and it's a recipe for disaster. Rams 31, Giants 17.

articles.title: Tennessee Titans vs. Philadelphia Eagles: Week 2 staff picks and predictions
articles.summary: The Titans Wire staff offer their picks and predictions ahead of a Week 2 game between the Tennessee Titans and Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans (0-1) will take on the Philadelphia Eagles (1-0) this Sunday afternoon at Nissa Stadium in their second game of the 2026 regular season.

Opening the week, the Titans were listed as 7-point home underdogs , and that's where the line remains as of this writing.

How does the Titans Wire staff see this Week 2 battle shaking out? Here's a look at our picks and score predictions.

The Titans come out and put on a better performance against the Eagles, but the Eagles' rushing attack eventually takes control before quarterback Jalen Hurts hits Dallas Goedert to pull away. Cam Ward is better, but it is nowhere near enough, and the Titans come up short.

There's really not much to say about the Titans anymore after their ridiculous loss to the Jets . They had no answer for Breece Hall , and even if Cedric Gray returns, they won't have an answer for Saquon Barkley . Simmons can't do it alone, and even if the line managed to slow Barkley down, I don't have much faith in the Titans' tackling ability outside of Anthony Hill. Offensively, I expect Cam Ward to be on the run for most of the game again. This line won't have an answer for Jalen Carter , and it's going to show.

The disappointing start to 2026 won't change on Sunday for the Titans. They're going up against a complete Eagles team who will steady their feet after an uneven Week 1 performance, and ultimately run away with things late. After the game, offensive coordinator Brian Daboll will say the performance wasn't good enough and that starts with him.

Call me crazy, but I think the Titans will be competitive this week. The Eagles' offense isn't quite the same without A.J. Brown . And we know Week 1 can be a little fluky sometimes. Now, I am not saying the Titans will be great this year, but I do think they look much better against a much stronger opponent. Ultimately, scoring against Philly's stout defense will be too difficult.

The Titans offense shows life after an abysmal Week 1 performance, with Cam Ward showing why he is franchise QB potential. However, the Titans' defensive secondary gives up a big play late to fall short to another 0-2 start.

The beginning of the Robert Saleh era could not have gotten off to a worse start. The Titans looked completely overwhelmed by a Jets team that was supposed to be in the same tier as them coming into the season. Now, Brian Daboll's offense has to figure out a way to move the ball against a Vic Fangio defense that is probably licking its chops. Saquon Barkley finds the end zone twice while the Titans fail to contain Dallas Goedert. It's going to be a long year in Nashville.

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals reveal development plan for QB Carson Beck
articles.summary: As the Cardinals' third-string quarterback, opportunities are limited for Carson Beck. Here is how Arizona is focusing on his development.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals have a math problem. Or, to be more accurate, a time problem.

With increasingly tight restrictions on NFL practices, opportunities are limited for their scout team. That group sees 32 live reps every Wednesday, 36 on Thursday and 20 on Friday.

And for backups, that's typically the only practice opportunity available in a given week. Unlike during training camp, the second-string units don't get regular work within the Cardinals' own scheme once the season begins. The third-stringers often get no work at all.

For the Cardinals, one of the key stories this season is the development of third-round rookie Carson Beck . Even as the third-string quarterback, he offers the Cardinals long-term upside at the sport's most important position, in a way that the veterans on their roster don't.

So with Beck, the Cardinals have come up with a plan. Rather than Gardner Minshew taking every scout team rep — as would typically be the case — they are now splitting their scout-team reps between Minshew and Beck.

See photos from Arizona Cardinals' season opener at LA Chargers

"Gardner's played a lot of football, and Carson hasn't, in the NFL," head coach Mike LaFleur said. "So as you're trying to develop these guys, we just thought it was right to do that. Had Gardner been a second-year guy and was our number two, then probably wouldn't be doing this."

"I get to go against our starting defense every day, which is awesome," Beck said. "And those are invaluable reps. So getting used to the speed, just developing and getting those reps. Obviously, if I was just sitting and not getting any reps, it's kind of hard to develop and grow."

The downside, of course, is that Beck isn't running the Cardinals' own scheme with the scout team, as he did during training camp. But he gets mental reps every day in meetings, both with the quarterbacks and with the full offense. And on the practice field, he's often running similar concepts to those that he would see on Sundays.

"Yeah, sure, it's not our offense," Beck said. "But everybody runs the 'same thing.' And you can make things translate and make them the same and go through reads the way that you would, even though it might not be exactly the same."

The ability to create those opportunities for Beck also helps mitigate the harm of the ribs injury he sustained in the Hall of Fame game.

Beck was the Cardinals' standout performer that night, completing 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown. After a rocky start to training camp, he looked in control of the Cardinals' offense, consistently making the right decisions, albeit against a defense that he admitted was "pretty vanilla."

The following week in practice, Beck continued to excel, most notably with a highlight-reel no-look touchdown pass that only served to accelerate the hype. But as that week progressed, his ribs injury got worse and worse. Eventually, he was shut down for two weeks and missed the Cardinals' final three preseason games.

"Obviously that part sucks, missing that time, which is just so valuable, catching up to speed in the NFL," Beck said. "But for me right now, it's just being the best that I can be in my role and doing whatever I can to help contribute to the team, and making sure that I'm prepared if my number is ever called."

Now that he's back on the field, Beck feels that his development has picked up where it left off back in August.

"You get around guys like LaFleur, (Nathaniel) Hackett, (Matt) Schaub and just pick their brains apart and the game just starts to slow down," Beck said.

The players he works with on the scout team have seen it, too.

"You can just tell," wide receiver Simi Fehoko said. "The guy can sling it, and he just has a good understanding of the game. Even in scout team, you'll see throws where you're like, 'I would never expect a rookie to make that throw.' And he did and completed it."

articles.title: Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr.’s Agent Pushing Envelope
articles.summary: Only time will tell when Joey Porter Jr. gets back on the field for the Pittsburgh Steelers, if at all. […]
articles.body:
Only time will tell when Joey Porter Jr. gets back on the field for the Pittsburgh Steelers , if at all. The Pittsburgh Steelers' standout cornerback is waiting on a new contract, with the situation having dragged on into the season.

Being that the Steelers traditionally don't talk deals once Week 1 rolls around, when and if Porter re-ups with his hometown team remains to be seen. His agent, Andre Odom, reminded the Steelers that he'd like to see his client in black and gold again soon, alongside fellow former Penn State product Jaquan Brisker .

"Admittedly, there is nothing I'd rather experience more than to see my two little brothers back together in the same secondary, again," Odom wrote Friday on X. "They made history in college. They'd certainly do it now."

They'd certainly do it now. 🙏🏾 @JoeyPorterJr @JaquanBrisker #LaFamilia pic.twitter.com/TbSqywU3pO — Certifiedadvisor (@AndreOdom) September 19, 2026

Certifiedadvisor (@AndreOdom) September 19, 2026

Brisker reposted the upload with two praying emojis and the eyes emoji. Brisker had an interception in his first game with the Steelers , last week's 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons at home.

"It was amazing," Brisker said of the crowd's reaction at Acrisure Stadium. "It's crazy, because I think last year, I dreamed of this moment. I'm so serious. I didn't know what team I was gonna be on, but literally, I literally had a dream of a pick in the middle of the field, and it came (true) today. It was actually crazy."

Porter, meanwhile, has been rumored to be a trade target, but the Steelers apparently haven't fielded any offers worth pulling the trigger on.

articles.title: The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly: Wake Forest Demon Deacons 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Miami was rolling then…..WHAT HAPPENED?!
articles.body:
Another game, another victory for the Canes! On Friday night, your Miami Hurricanes continued the ACC schedule, traveling to Winston-Salem, NC to play, and beat, the Wake Forest Demon Deacons 33-20.

AND Mike Schiffman is back with the 3 stars of the game:

And with no further ado, let's get into this edition of The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly:

A win! I will never take this for granted.

QB Darian Mensah . 30/34 passing, 220 yards, 3 touchdowns, 0 interceptions

Mensah's cumulative stats this year: 71/79 passing, 90% completions, 873 yards, 11 touchdowns, 0 interceptions.

WR Malachi Toney . 12 catches for 114 yards and a touchdown.

Toney's cumulative stats: 28 catches for 444 yards and 5 touchdowns.

RB Mark Fletcher Jr. 16 carries for 85 yards and a touchdown.

S J.J. Dunnigan. 8 tackles, 3 QB hurries, and another great game from my favorite player.

CB Ethan O'Connor. 8 tackles, solid coverage, and the game-winning interception. Bravo.

The defensive line. EDGEs Armondo Blount, Marquise Lightfoot, and Damon Wilson II finally made their presence felt. DTs Justin Scott and Ahmad Moten Sr. also played very very well.

In total, the DL combined for 13 tackles, 3 sacks, and 3.5 TFLs. Oh, and forced 3 holding penalties, which could have easily been tripled. There was pressure all day long, and solid run defense as well. It wasn't perfect, but this was a big step forward for the defensive line.

Miami walking 92 yards down the field in 14 plays to score on the first drive of the game. Great choices from Mensah, solid play all around, and in the end, a touchdown. That'll work.

That drive ended with this 9-yard touchdown pass from Mensah to WR Joshua Moore .

Mark Fletcher Jr. running dudes over!!!!!! Or, in the words of Marshawn Lynch : RUN THRU A MUFUCKA'S FACE!!!!!

Mensah to TE Elija Lofton for a 21 yard score. Y-leak. Wide open. Easy as you like. (and look at Mensah's opening stats after 2 drives. LOL my goodness)

EDGE Damon Wilson II with his first sack as a Hurricane!

LB Mo Toure with a MASSIVE hit to force a fumble, which would have been Miami's first takeaway of the year but there was a penalty away from the ball.

Scoring touchdowns on the first 3 drives of the night.

Scoring on 5 of our first 6 offensive drives.

Forcing Wake Forest into 3-and-outs on their final 4 first half drives.

Forcing Wake Forest's final 3 drives to end as follows: downs at the Miami 14, Downs at the Wake 42, and an interception from the Miami 22.

4-4 scoring in the redzone (all touchdowns)

Mensah 220 yards on 30 completions? Woof.

I know Wake Forest was trying to play zone to take away the super explosive plays….but they went to man-to-man schemes in the 2nd half and Miami did nothing against them. Can't have that. That's bad.

No Jordan Lyle, despite him being dressed for the game, and Miami losing the top 2 backs on the depth chart. His de-facto suspension continues.

7 penalties for 75 yards. Nowhere NEAR good enough.

Whatever the FUCK happened after we went up 31-7. Kill it with fire.

No seriously, I'm trying to understand what happened. Miami's offense was walking up and down the field, then did less than nothing on the final 6 drives of the game. Truly baffling.

After going up 31-7, these were Miami's next 4 drives:

And the next drive after those 4? 4 plays, 6 yards, no first downs, and a blocked FG from 54 yards. TRULY terrible stuff.

Injuries. Injuries. And more injuries. Seriously, somebody reset the sliders or something.

ALL the missed sacks on Gio Lopez . Credit to him for being a tough player and elusive to a point, but there were a lot of bad plays on Miami's part that enabled him to extend plays.

Cam Pruitt with a holding penalty on the opening kick return of the game. C'mon man.

Mark Fletcher Jr. with a block in the back on an early screen to Daylyn Upshaw. Gotta play clean!

DT Ahmad Moten Sr. leaving the game early with a left shoulder injury. You truly hate to see it. Damnit.

DL Armondo Blount called for a weak roughing the passer to gift Wake Forest extra yards on top of a completion.

Miami's defense gave up their first touchdown of the year on Wake's first drive.

Again, whatever that was after Miami went up 31-7. I'm very upset by the deterioration of the offense, and the penalties that allowed Wake to move down the field and score on the defense.

RB Marty Brown suffering what the broadcast called a "gruesome" knee injury on a 32 yard run midway through the 2nd quarter. Brown is Miami's Swiss Army Knife backup RB. Losing him would hurt the depth, but present opportunities for others. Still, you HATE to see injuries. UGH.

This is the play where Brown sustained his injury

TE Elija Lofton went down with a left leg (ankle?) injury late in the 2nd quarter. TURN OFF INJURIES.

RB Mark Fletcher Jr. missing/not attempting a block vs the blitz, leading to a sack of Darian Mensah. Great player, ugly play

EDGE Damon Wilson II called for roughing the passer to negate Miami's first takeaway of the year, a forced fumble my LB Mo Toure on a MASSIVE hit against the Wake RB.

Wake Forest had a guy ALL ALONE on 4th and 5. It was incomplete, but had they seen this, it's a touchdown. Bottom of the picture below, just above the "33" on the scorebug.

I'm just…..disappointed. The lack of focus. The penalties. The stagnation on offense. The PENALTIES. The missed sacks. The injuries. THE PENALTIES. I know we won by 2 touchdowns but this was nowhere near good enough.

Offense : First 6 drives: A+; Last 6 drives: F

Truly a Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde performance. Miami had a plan and answers for Wake's zone scheme to be methodical, consistent, slightly explosive, and go up and down the field easily to build a 31-7 lead.

And then invasion of the body snatchers happened and Miami's offense went into a shell, and had 4 consecutive 3-and-outs and a 4 play drive that ended with a blocked FG before the final drive where they FINALLY converted a 1st down to secure the victory.

I know there were injuries, but Miami has too much talent for this to happen on offense. Mensah looked dinged up, but I'm sure Miami won't say he was. Malachi Toney was on a pitch count after straining his abdominals stretching for a catch late in the second quarter. STILL, the fact that Miami's offense turned into…..whatever it was that we watched after the 1st drive of the second half is unacceptable. Full stop.

Defensive line actually showed a pulse which is great. But there were issues with Mo Toure and Omar Thornton , both players who have been questioned for their coverage abilities, giving up touchdowns on the same slot fade concept. And there were a metric ton of missed tackles, SPECIFICALLY sack opportunities on Lopez. Yes, the defense was able to step up and get stops late in the game when they were needed, yes they were able to get stops early, but there is still MUCH to be desired here.

Penalty on the opening kick return of the game. Good punting when we used it but we used it too much for my liking, especially given the early production from the offense. Add in a missed/blocked FG, and yeah, that isn't a showing anybody is excited about.

I almost feel like Mario Cristobal's continual statements about middling teams being better than they are was a self fulfilling prophecy tonight. Wake is FINE, but Miami is a clear class better than them…..or was for 34 minutes of the game. Then, Miami went into a shell, let Wake hang around, and that just wasn't at all necessary.

Let me be clear: it wasn't the INTENT of the coaching staff or offense to play poorly and let Wake hang around, but it felt like that was the impact.

Operationally, the offense played a clean game. The only offensive penalty was a questionable block in the back call on Mark Fletcher Jr. And, for the first 34 minutes of the game, the offense was unstoppable. But then there were missed blocks. And *VERY* conservative play calls (all the screens), and some poor play (WOOF, offensive line), and things grinded to a halt. Dawson had answers, then didn't. And he has to find something to settle the team and get a first down — which Miami had exactly *ONE* of in the final 27 minutes of the game across 6 possessions. It came 3 plays from the end of the game to give Miami the chance to go to victory formation.

Wake Forest came out to open the game and walked down the field for a 75 yard TD drive to tie the score. In that moment, I said I needed adjustments from DC Corey Hetherman. And I got them. Miami forced 4 consecutive 3-and-outs thereafter and built the big lead we've been talking about. I liked the late adjustment to put J.J. Dunnigan at LB and spy Lopez. I liked the unceasing blitzes from the slot (regardless of who was assigned the blitz). I liked the pressure the defensive line got. I liked the variety of players at linebacker, all of whom had some nice moments.

Overall, I thought the defensive scheme was fine, but the inability to complete sacks — seriously, Lopez stepped out of at least 8 MORE sacks than we saw — and ALL. THE. PENALTIES — 6 of Miami's 7 penalties came on defense — were the issues. Like with the offense, it wasn't the intent of the coaches to have that performance from the players, but that's what we got, and it wasn't good enough.

I'll admit that this is a harsh grade. But if the standard and goal is to compete for championships, high standards and tough feedback are required.

That's it for this installment of The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly.

Hop in the comments and let me know your thoughts.

articles.title: Mazzola: the legend of Sandro in 10 matches
articles.summary: What makes a player special? Is it their skill, their goals? Or perhaps a distinctive trademark, such as a shirt number or a pair of moustaches recognisable...
articles.body:
What makes a player special? Is it their skill, their goals? Or perhaps a distinctive trademark, such as a shirt number or a pair of moustaches recognisable among thousands of others? Maybe it is a long career spent wearing just one shirt?

What if it was all of these things that made Sandro Mazzola unique? Player, captain, one-club man, timeless symbol. But above all, a good man, just as he wanted to be remembered. A good man who lived his life with Inter and for Inter: a 'mother' to little Sandro, to whom he gave back all the love he had received and more at different moments and stages of his life.

The first of these is the most famous, the most unforgettable, and the one upon which his life was built: a life that began as an Inter player and saw him make 565 appearances in the Nerazzurri shirt. To us, Mazzola is a symbol, a shining star who paved the way for everyone who came after him. To understand what he represents, we want to tell you about the ten most significant matches of Sandro's Nerazzurri career.

"LIKE THAT 9-1" — JUVENTUS-INTER, SERIE A 1960/61

Turin, 10 June 1961. Inter had to travel to Juventus for a match that had, in fact, already been played. The game was originally scheduled for 16 April but was abandoned following a pitch invasion. After initially awarding Inter the win by default, a result that would have been decisive in the title race, it was decided on 3 June that the match would have to be replayed from the beginning. In protest, president Angelo Moratti decided to send the De Martino side, the team that was once known as the Primavera. Among the young Nerazzurri was one particularly promising player: Sandro Mazzola, 18 years old, who nevertheless had some very important school exams coming up. His teammates insisted that he come to Turin and play alongside them. Sandro obtained permission from the headmaster, asking him to consider that this might be his only ever Serie A appearance, and took to the pitch against Juventus, who had just been crowned Italian champions. The match was completely one-sided: it finished 9-1, with Omar Sívori scoring six goals. But Inter's only goal had a special signature: Mazzola himself scored it from the penalty spot. A debut and a goal against Juventus, in a match that would prove highly significant in shaping Inter's identity. It would certainly not be Sandro's last appearance.

13 SECONDS — INTER 1-1 MILAN, SERIE A 1962/63

Sandro's first full season with Inter's first team. It was a special year, with Herrera's side battling Juventus for the Scudetto, a triumph that president Angelo Moratti had been chasing for some time. Mazzola was 20 years old, still very young, but he was already a key figure for the Mago in the dugout. He wore the number 8 shirt and would normally have played as an inside forward, but Herrera fashioned a role specifically for him, somewhere between a forward and a midfielder, to make the most of his outstanding goalscoring ability. On 24 February 1963, Inter faced Milan in the return derby. It was the first derby of Sandro's career, having missed the first meeting of the season. Kick-off: Di Giacomo to Mazzola, Mazzola to Suárez. A ball is played deep to Corso on the left, who feeds Mazzola, and he immediately lays it back to Suárez. Luisito finds Sandro again, all alone inside the Milan box: goal, 1-0 after just 13 seconds. The fastest goal in the history of the derby, to this day, on the occasion of his first match against Milan. The game finished 1-1 after Sani's equaliser, but Mazzola's 13 seconds went down in Italian football history.

VALENTINO'S SHIRT — INTER 1-1 TORINO, SERIE A 1962/63

A historic day, in a match unlike any other for Sandro. Inter face Torino at San Siro on the final day of the Serie A season. The Nerazzurri had already won the Scudetto on 5 May, but the match against the Granata was an opportunity to celebrate. This was where the success story of the Grande Inter began: Herrera and Moratti's first title, and the first league championship after nine years of waiting. It was also the first time Sandro faced Torino. At the start of the match, Granata captain Enzo Bearzot presented him with a shirt that had belonged to Valentino Mazzola, Sandro's father and the star of Grande Torino who died at Superga in 1949. Mazzola scored a goal to finish the season with 11 league goals, making him Inter's joint top scorer alongside Di Giacomo. Ferrini's equaliser was significant only for the record books: the Nerazzurri fans' celebrations could begin. From Grande Torino to Grande Inter, the only two Italian teams ever to be given that distinction — and always with the Mazzola family at the heart of the story.

"PUSKÁS' WORDS" — INTER 3-1 REAL MADRID , EUROPEAN CUP 1963/64

The Grande Inter's first European season was a triumph: the Nerazzurri won their first European Cup at Vienna's Prater on 27 May 1964. But their opponents were no ordinary side: it was Alfredo Di Stéfano and Ferenc Puskás' Real Madrid, the team that had left an indelible mark on football history. Mazzola was just 21 when he played in the final. The emotion was overwhelming. In the tunnel before going out onto the pitch, Sandro was mesmerised by the Real Madrid stars. It was up to Suárez to snap him out of it: "We're going out to play the final — do you want to stand here watching Alfredo?" Mazzola certainly went out and played that final: he scored twice, took Inter to the top of European football and established himself once and for all as a truly world-class player. The most important seal of approval came from Puskás, who gave him his shirt: "I played against your father. You are worthy of him."

VICTORY FOR "LA BELLA" — INTER-INDEPENDIENTE, SECOND LEG OF THE 1964 INTERCONTINENTAL CUP FINAL

From Europe to the world, the myth of the Grande Inter continued to grow. Winning the European Cup earned the Nerazzurri a meeting with Argentina 's Independiente for the Intercontinental Cup, which at the time was played over two legs. At Avellaneda on 9 September, a genuine battle unfolded, with Independiente winning 1-0. The return leg was scheduled for Milan two weeks later. Inter had to win to force la bella , the decisive play-off for the trophy. It took just eight minutes to change the course of history. As always, it was Sandro Mazzola who stepped up, breaking the deadlock. The second goal arrived towards the end of the first half, scored by Mario Corso. Inter won and earned the right to contest the play-off, which was held in Madrid and decided in extra time by another Corso goal.

"WHEN THE SAINTS GO MARCHING IN" — INTER-LIVERPOOL 3-0, EUROPEAN CUP 1964/65

How do you complete an impossible comeback? With character and a touch of madness. In 1965, Inter, the reigning European champions, were looking to repeat the previous year's achievement. In the semi-finals, the Nerazzurri faced Liverpool . At Anfield, the Reds won 3-1, with Sandro scoring Inter's goal. A comeback was needed. Inter had to overturn a daunting deficit against Bill Shankly's formidable English side, who had celebrated by blasting out When the Saints Go Marching In . Mazzola had an idea: he handed the San Siro announcer the 33 rpm record featuring Louis Armstrong's version of the song, asking him to play it after Inter's victory. And so it was. In the eighth minute, Corso opened the scoring. A minute later, Joaquín Peiró brilliantly robbed goalkeeper Lawrence of the ball and made it 2-0. The decisive goal came in the second half from Giacinto Facchetti: 3-0, comeback complete. Inter had won. San Siro had won, more electrifying than ever. When the Saints Go Marching In rang out at full volume around the stadium. Sandro had been right.

TWO GOALS FOR THE SECOND CUP — INTER 3-0 INDEPENDIENTE, INTERCONTINENTAL CUP 1965

The comeback against Liverpool opened the door to the second European Cup final. At San Siro, against Benfica and in torrential rain, Jair scored the only goal of the game. European champions once again, and once again facing Independiente in the Intercontinental Cup. This time, the tie got off to a positive start. At San Siro on 8 September 1965, Inter won the first leg 3-0. Peiró opened the scoring in the third minute, but the star of the show was Mazzola. In the 22nd minute, he scored at the end of a spectacular Nerazzurri attacking move. Then came the masterpiece in the second half: Sandro scored an overhead kick that finally put the Argentinians to the sword. In the return leg, Independiente could only manage a 0-0 draw. Inter were world champions for the second consecutive year.

THE GOLDEN STAR — INTER 4-1 LAZIO , SERIE A 1965/66

A dominant league campaign, a season in which Inter powered towards the Scudetto at full speed. Napoli , Milan and Bologna tried to put pressure on the Nerazzurri, but there was no stopping them. The title was mathematically secured on 15 May 1966, in the penultimate league game against Lazio at San Siro. Suárez opened the scoring early in the second half, before Renna equalised. Mazzola restored Inter's lead in the 63rd minute, followed by an own goal from Governato and a Domenghini strike. The match finished 4-1. Inter were Italian champions, but this was no ordinary Scudetto. It was the tenth in Nerazzurri history: Inter had earned their First Star, 58 years after the Club's foundation and 58 years before the arrival of the Second. Curious numbers that repeated themselves, with Sandro always at the heart of the story. He scored 19 goals in the 1965/66 league campaign.

THE TABLE — INTER-MILAN 2-0, SERIE A 1970/71

Mazzola's story went well beyond the Grande Inter era. Sandro became a leading figure in a new winning cycle, a veteran of a revamped side seeking fresh success. Alongside him were Burgnich, Facchetti and Corso, helping to guide a new generation of champions such as Boninsegna. Mazzola was now Inter captain and one of the team's defining figures. The season, however, began badly, with Napoli and AC Milan pulling clear at the top of the table. Nerazzurri coach Heriberto Herrera was dismissed, with Gianni Invernizzi promoted from the Primavera. And so the legendary table of the Nerazzurri veterans was born, led by Mazzola: a series of predictions for Inter's results and those of their rivals, creating a roadmap that would have to be followed if they were to mount a comeback. One of the key turning points came in the derby on 7 March 1971. In the 12th minute, Corso scored from a free-kick, before Mazzola doubled the lead with a header after making the most of a Boninsegna lay-off. The match finished 2-0, with Inter now breathing down Milan's neck in the table. The table would be followed to the letter, and the Scudetto arrived on 2 May with a 5-0 victory over Foggia.

THE LAST ONE — MILAN 2-0 INTER, COPPA ITALIA 1976/77

Sixteen years after making his debut against Juventus, Mazzola brought his career as an Inter player to an end. He did so in a derby that doubled as the Coppa Italia final, on 3 July 1977: white shirt, number 10 on his back and the captain's armband around his arm. At the centre of the pitch, he exchanged greetings with Gianni Rivera, the Rossoneri captain — his counterpart and the other half of Italy 's famous "relay" at the 1970 World Cup in Mexico. The match ended in a Milan victory, with the Coppa Italia going to the Rossoneri. But all eyes and applause were for Sandro, who marked the end of his playing career with a quotation from Dante: "It is willed there where what is willed can be done; and ask no more." And so Mazzola's playing career came to an end, while a new chapter began one that would see him become a major figure as a director, forever bound to the Nerazzurri colours.

That day, Sandro said goodbye to Inter and to his people. Now it is our turn to pay tribute to him and thank him for everything he has been throughout his life. A good man, above all.

articles.title: 3 X-Factors for the Browns clash with the Buccaneers in Week 2
articles.summary: Week 2’s Cleveland Browns versus TB Bucs is not just about Baker Mayfield, Deshaun Watson. A few X-Factors also matter
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns will try to finish their two-game Florida road trip on a positive note as the team will travel to Tampa Bay to play the Buccaneers this Sunday . For the Browns, it's all about trying to bounce back after a rough season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars . As a collective, the Browns didn't play well at all, and it doesn't get much easier as they will play a Buccaneers team that will have a highly motivated quarterback in Baker Mayfield .

Here are three X-Factors for Browns vs Bucs in Week 2:

In terms of debuts for coordinators in new situations, both Zac Robinson and Mike Rutenberg would've like to have done things differently. However, if people don't know by now, Rutenberg and Robinson have history. Both Robinson and Rutenberg were with the Atlanta Falcons last year under former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris (who is now the San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator). Robinson was the offensive coordinator and Rutenberg was the defensive passing game coordinator.

Robinson had his issues against the Cincinnati Bengals , mainly in terms of communication when it came to relaying the plays, but he called a somewhat competent game. Rutenberg, on the other hand, struggled. The Browns defense spent more time playing zone coverage rather than man coverage, which led to frequent coverage busts. The players have to execute, but the defensive coordinator has to put the players in better situations.

Familiarity is well known between the two, but Rutenberg has to call a better game defensively and make life difficult for Tampa Bay 's offense.

In terms of matchups, this one will be one to monitor. Browns cornerback Denzel Ward was the only cornerback that played well last week against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Cornerback Myles Harden struggled mightily, while Tyson Campbell 's performance wasn't nearly as poor as Harden's; it wasn't great.

This week doesn't get any easier. Ward will likely be matched up with Buccaneers wide receiver Emeka Egbuka , Campbell will likely be tasked against Jalen McMillan or rookie Ted Hurst, Myles Harden will be tasked against Chris Godwin . It's hard to imagine the secondary playing any worse than they did last week but the Bucs have versatility in the wide receiver room.

Campbell's questionable status for the game could create other issues.

It's possible that the cornerbacks will have to play more zone due to the lack of a consistent pass rush. It's not necessarily ideal, but due to the pass rush not being there, they might not have a choice.

By the Browns standards, their defensive line didn't perform to the level that they are capable of in Week 1.

The pass rush was nonexistent, and the run defense was questionable at best. Tampa's offensive line had an uneven performance, as the pass blocking wasn't up to standard, but the run blocking was solid in their opening contest. As for the Browns, the pass rush needs to be better. It's simple as that. Pressure was going to fall off after the team traded away Myles Garrett ; it's the reality of the situation. However, Jared Verse , who they traded for in the Garrett deal, wasn't the best defensive lineman for the Browns that day. That was Mason Graham .

Aside from quarterback play, the game will be determined in the trenches, and both units (who had lackluster debuts) will look for redemption this week.

The young Newcastle United stars have hammered Sunderland on Saturday.

The United stars of the future having travelled to play at the Academy of Light for an 11am kick-off.

The Mackem lights started flickering when Charlie Robinson put the Newcastle United Under 18s 1-0 up on 31 minutes.

Then it became very dark for the young Mackems when within two minutes of the second half kicking off, Noah Morgan doubled the lead.

It was lights off altogether for the hosts when substitute Theo Benjamin made it three on 82 minutes, only six minutes after coming off the bench.

What a week for the son of former striker Trevor Benjamin, as he has scored three goals against Sunderland in less than a week!

Sunderland hosted Newcastle United in the Under 17s Premier League Cup on Tuesday and United hammered them 4-1.

Theo Benjamin got two in that victory, with Jack Skelton and Jayden Koussou getting the other goals.

Today's league win means it is five victories in six for the Newcastle United Under 18s and having scored 19 goals in the half dozen league games, they are behind only Manchester City in the Premier League North Under 18s table.

Great to see the investment in youth paying off after a decade and a half of Mike Ashley refusing to allow a single penny to be spent unless forced to.

To cap it all, on Friday FOUR Newcastle United young stars were named in the latest England Under 18s squad.

articles.title: Indiana Pacers Reportedly Plan to Take It Slow With Tyrese Haliburton This Upcoming Season
articles.summary: Tyrese Haliburton is expected to suit up for the Indiana Pacers this year after missing the entire 2025-26 campaign due to a torn Achilles. But according to...
articles.body:
Tyrese Haliburton is expected to suit up for the Indiana Pacers this year after missing the entire 2025-26 campaign due to a torn Achilles. But according to ESPN's Jamal Collier, fans should temper their expectations upon his return.

"Haliburton led the Pacers to back-to-back conference finals trips in 2024 and '25 and was one game away from winning the championship, but will his presence once again immediately vault Indiana back into the conversation among the East's contenders?" Collier wrote.

"He has had extended time to recover and said recently he has been chomping at the bit to get back on the court. Indiana may take it slow with their superstar to start the season, with the hope that come playoff time, the Pacers will be in position to shock the league again," he added.

Haliburton's absence was keenly felt, as the Indiana Pacers finished 19-63 last season – good for second-worst in the Eastern Conference. Since then, the team retooled its roster, including swapping Bennedict Mathurin for Ivica Zubac and signing Larry Nance Jr. and Kelly Oubre in free agency.

Indiana Pacers News: Insider has optimistic outlook for the team in 2026-27

Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star recently appeared on CLNS Media's Celtics Daily with Bobby Manning, where he predicted that the Indiana Pacers can win 48 to 50 games in the 2026-27 regular season.

"A key thing to remember here, as far as Eastern standings, they won the East off a four seed in 2024-25. They got to the (Eastern Conference) Finals out of a six (seed) in 2023-24. They're good for leaving some regular-season wins on the table, basically. They have done that in the past. In each of those runs, they found a different gear once they got to postseason basketball," Dopirak said.

"They obviously know that they've gotta be top six. I don't think they want anything to do with the Play-In round whatsoever," he continued. "But I think they're certainly a team that says if we're top-6, we can get wherever we want. It's just a question of getting it, being able to play their style of basketball. Is it a team that's good enough to win 48 to 50 games? I think it is."

articles.title: Expect traffic downtown for national paddle boarding competition in Gig Harbor
articles.summary: The USA SUP National Championships 2026 are taking place Sept. 18-20.
articles.body:
Downtown Gig Harbor will be busier than usual this weekend while athletes race kayaks, surfskis, stand-up paddleboards and other watercraft in the harbor.

From Friday to Sunday, the city is hosting athletes from across the country for the USA SUP National Championships 2026 . The competition organizers are partnering with The Narrows Challenge, an annual race sponsored by the Gig Harbor Canoe & Kayak Racing Team .

The Narrows Challenge is in its sixth year and takes place on Saturday, said Tod Cole, one of the team's coaches. Cole is acting as co-race director of the Narrows Challenge this year with USA SUP board member Kristin Thomas. The race takes athletes on a route from the Gig Harbor Lighthouse to Point Fosdick and back. The Narrows Challenge is open to all open watercraft, not just stand-up paddleboarders, he told The News Tribune.

The Gig Harbor Canoe & Kayak Racing Team, which holds 11 national titles, got connected with USA SUP after the paddleboarding organization asked to hold their event in Gig Harbor, Cole said. The team worked closely with the city and with Visit Gig Harbor (the tourism arm of the Gig Harbor Chamber of Commerce) to prepare for the event.

"I'm excited to see the Gig Harbor community see an increase in water sports activities since we have such a great opportunity here with what we've been provided," Cole said.

Gig Harbor Public Works Director Jeff Langhelm wrote in an email that the downtown area will be busy during the competition.

"For the Narrows Challenge and SUP Nationals, the community can expect increased traffic, crowds, and parking demand throughout downtown during the weekend, especially around Skansie Park and near Old Ferry Landing Park," he wrote. "Drivers should plan ahead, allow extra travel time, and use caution when traveling through the area."

Cold said there won't be any road closures for the event, and two local churches have signage allowing attendees to park in their lots. Police will be on-site for safety during the event, he said.

The event will also feature live music from two bands (Bards of Paradise and The Profits), a drone show from the Peninsula School District and food trucks on Saturday evening.

Thomas said the event includes sprints, endurance races and a technical course. Qualifiers from the national championships will represent the United States at the 2026 ICF Stand Up Paddling (SUP) World Championships in Sabaudia, Italy, said Thomas.

articles.title: Pullman dominates St. Maries en route to perfect 3-0 start
articles.summary: Sep. 19—PULLMAN — Pullman defensive lineman Nata Fotofili said the Greyhounds coaching staff preach to the players to "establish dominance." The Hounds could...
articles.body:
Sep. 19—PULLMAN — Pullman defensive lineman Nata Fotofili said the Greyhounds coaching staff preach to the players to "establish dominance."

The Hounds could not have looked all that much more dominant Friday night in their 49-6 win over the St. Maries Lumberjacks at Hobbs Field at Pullman High School for their first 3-0 start since the 2018 season.

"The biggest thing is just (that) the community's proud of what's going on and are invested," Pullman coach Kevin Agnew said of the 3-0 start.

On the Hounds' first offensive possession, Joshua Ratliff carried the ball 52 yards for the score. Ratliff scored two more times, both near the goal line, and finished with 105 yards on just six carries.

Agnew said in the preseason that Ratliff would be the premier back. Friday night, the senior back showcased his ability to thrive between the tackles and get to the second level on multiple chunk runs.

This is Ratliff's first season on varsity football, as he missed the previous two seasons with back-to-back shoulder surgeries, but feels he's starting to shake off the rust.

"I've been rusty; it's taken me a lot to figure out how to ready my blocks and how to break tackles, but I'm getting better every week," Ratliff said.

Pullman quarterback Griffen Engle came out at the 6:46 mark of the second quarter and did not leave any points on the table. The Hounds came away with touchdowns on all five of their starting offense's possessions.

Engle's highlight play of the game came on a 36-yard run. He faked the give to Ratliff and plunged forward, breaking three tackles on the way to cross the end zone for the game's second score.

"Thought (the starting offense) did a really nice job," Agnew said. "Those are tough games to be in on both sides, and hats off to St. Maries for continuing to fight and putting one in there at the end. I was happy with how our offense came out and worked."

Through three games, the Hounds have allowed 12 combined points, and their performance against St. Maries Friday night looked perhaps their most dominant. The Lumberjacks felt the size of Pullman from the jump.

On the Lumberjacks' first offensive snap, Pullman defensive lineman Siua Fotofili blew up the exchange between the center and quarterback Gavin Durham. On second down, Engle recorded a sack, and the Hounds forced an incompletion on third down.

The Lumberjacks went three-and-out on their next possession and on the ensuing punt, Nata Fotofili got his hands on a blocked punt.

"I feel like (the defense has) a lot of chemistry that we had from last year and because of that chemistry we're able to go dominate, go execute, stuff like that," Nata Fotofili said. "I feel like our discipline is on a great level; elite defenses is what our coaches strive for."

The Greyhounds have enjoyed the presence of multiple key starters returning, and the group has only built on their end from last season. Over Pullman's last nine games, including six from last season, the Hounds are 7-2.

articles.summary: Everything you need to know ahead of a blockbuster weekend of competition in Copenhagen
articles.body:
Jakob Ingebrigtsen headlines a starry field of contenders as nearly 500 athletes head to Copenhagen for the annual World Athletics Road Running Championships.

The Norwegian great is targeting a first world title on the road having entered the 5k after claiming European and Ultimate Championships gold in the event. But he'll face stiff competition from 10,000m world champion Jimmy Gressier, with the Frenchman having set a world-leading time of 12:51 over the shorter distance.

The USA's Yared Nuguse leads the contenders in the mile, while the men's half marathon field is headlined by double Olympic gold medallist Joshua Cheptegei of Uganda and Sweden's world 10,000m silver medallist Andreas Almgren.

Kenya's Agnes Ngetich is aiming for the cross-country and road double this season as she targets victory in the half marathon with Ethiopia's Likina Amebaw, who claimed a brilliant win in the 5km at the Ultimate Championships last weekend, going for two world titles in successive weekends.

When are the World Athletics Road Running Championships?

The World Athletics Road Running Championships take place in Copenhagen, Denmark on Saturday 19 and Sunday 20 September 2026, with six world titles to be decided in the men's and women's mile, 5km and half marathon.

Viewers in the UK can watch the championships live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app.

articles.title: Beating Baker Mayfield would be a big deal for Browns, fans
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns history with Baker Mayfield brings some extra feelings in this Week 2 Bucs matchup.
articles.body:
Baker Mayfield's journey has been a massive part of the Cleveland Browns' story over the past decade. The Browns' decision to trade for Deshaun Watson marked the end of the Mayfield era in Cleveland. The animosity between Mayfield and members of the organization continued during the years following the trade, making this a very interesting game. The last time Mayfield played against the Browns was in September of 2022, his first game as the starting quarterback for the Carolina Panthers.

A win this week would not just be about Mayfield. The team is looking to bounce back after a very tough Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars . They are looking to show that this loss does not define who they are as a team. The defense needs to put together a solid performance this week after a disjointed Week 1. After Mayfield fumbled a career-high three times in Week 1, the Cleveland defense will hope to create turnovers and give its offense chances to succeed.

Many of Mayfield's teammates and coaching staff from his time in Cleveland are no longer with the organization, so there won't be many personal feelings from players in the organization during this matchup. The personal feelings will mostly lie with the fans. While the trade still brings mixed emotions for many fans, it gives them an additional reason to want a win this week, even if that too will create mixed emotions.

Auburn leads the all-time series between the schools 43-39-2 dating to 1912 and has won three of the last four meetings. However, the last time they met in 2019, Florida won 24-13 in the Swamp, adding to the Gators' 11-2 record that year.

articles.title: 5 takeaways from Oregon Ducks' dominant 84-0 win over Portland State
articles.summary: Our five biggest takeaways from the Oregon Ducks' 84-0 blowout win over the Portland State Vikings on Friday night.
articles.body:
On Friday night, it was all smiles in Autzen Stadium after the Oregon Ducks walked off the field with a historic win in their hands following an 84-0 defeat of the Portland State Vikings. It was the most points in Oregon Ducks ' modern program history , and the largest margin of victory ever inside Autzen Stadium.

Considering that just six days ago, Oregon suffered arguably the worst loss of the Dan Lanning era, this win felt a bit cathartic, regardless of the opponent.

"We have a better team, and no disrespect for Portland State, but that's the way it should look when we execute the way we should execute," Lanning said after the game.

While this win in no way rights all of Oregon's wrongs so far this season, and doesn't prove that they are ready to earn a spot in the College Football Playoff, it does do something for the confidence and gets things back on the right track ahead of next week's monstrous matchup against the USC Trojans.

Here are our five biggest takeaways from the day:

I get it. This was Portland State, an 0-3 FCS school that has no business being on the same field as the Ducks, all due respect. Any takeaways from this game need to come with a massive disclaimer. I understand.

That being said, I think this had to feel pretty good for Oregon fans . After the way the first two weeks transpired for the Ducks, it feels as if Oregon fans would have happily seen their team go up against the South Eugene football team — RIP — just in order to see some semblance of execution once again. It doesn't matter who the opponent is; all that matters is the Ducks were able to line up and remember what it feels like to have success.

There's an old saying in basketball that sometimes, a shooter simply needs to see the ball go through the hoop in order to get out of a slump, whether that comes from a layup or a free throw. I asked Dan Lanning on Friday night if there was any similarities between that and what the Ducks were able to do offensively against the Vikings , putting up 726 total yards and scoring touchdowns on 12 of their 13 drives.

"It certainly doesn't hurt," Lanning said in response.

No matter how curt his answer, I do believe this is something worth considering for the Ducks. After being stagnant for two straight weeks, the Ducks got to feel joy offensively on Friday night. Sure, it may mean nothing in the grand scheme of things, and doesn't accurately portray what this offense may be able to do against the likes of USC, Ohio State, or Michigan , but maybe playing free for a single night was enough to kick things back into high gear.

For Duck fans, I think it was important. No longer were fans complaining about play calls and arguing over which position unit was more disappointing. For a single night, Oregon fans were having fun again, and after the week that we've had in Eugene, I think that's important.

Before we get too far, let me just be up front and clear about one thing: There is absolutely no quarterback competition or controversy in Eugene, and if the Ducks are going to reach their potential this year, it's going to be on the back of Dante Moore .

Now, with that being said, I think it's fair to admit that Dylan Raiola looked fantastic on Friday night, and it should be incredibly encouraging for Oregon fans.

Coming in at the start of the third quarter with Oregon already up 42-0, Raiola was quite literally perfect, completing 11-of-11 passes for 124 yards and three touchdowns. He led a trio of perfect drives and found TE Andrew Olesh, WR Messiah Hampton, and WR Brady Bidwell all on impressive throws to help balloon the lead.

Again, this means very little for the 2026 season, barring something happening to Moore, but when it comes to Oregon's future, Duck fans should take note. We've had a sense that this season was virtually a tryout for Raiola, seeing if he was capable of being the starter in 2027, or if Lanning would have to go into the transfer portal once again. If Friday night was any indication — yes, I know, the disclaimer about Portland State and the level of competition — I think fans are pretty excited for a potential Raiola era down the road.

At long last, we got a non-conference game where the outcome was well in hand, giving fans an opportunity to see the depth of this roster. On Friday night, the young guys got a chance to play, and they absolutely showed out. In general, it was the 2026 recruiting class that stole the show, but freshmen and redshirt freshmen across the board had outsized impacts in this one. I don't have the time to do a detailed analysis of every underclassman to see the field, but here are some guys who really stood out to me, in no particular order:

RB Brandon Smith: 16 carries, 71 yards, 1 TD

RB Tradarian Ball: 7 carries, 47 yards, 1 TD

WR Messiah Hampton: 6 catches, 71 yards, 2 TDs

TE Kendre Harrison: 4 catches, 53 yards, 1 TD

TE Andrew Olesh: 2 catches, 23 yards, 1 TD

S Jett Washington: 2 INTs, 1 forced fumble

There are many more guys who deserve mention, including both linemen Immanuel Iheanacho and Tommy Tofi, but at the top, I was really impressed by all of these guys. It was great to finally see Oregon in a blowout, giving us a chance to dissect the depth of the roster and get excited about the future.

Alright, we've gushed enough about this game; let's finish out with a couple of real items.

There were a lot of things I saw on Friday night that were improved for the Ducks, but I don't think the defensive line was one of them. Yet again, Oregon's front four of Matayo Uiagalelei , Teitum Tuioti , Bear Alexander , and A'Mauri Washington struggled to get home on pass rushes and failed to record a sack. Between the four of them, only Alexander had 0.5 tackles for loss. I understand that the Vikings were running a quick passing game and were getting the ball out with pace before a rush could get home, but this was still a game where I wanted to see the defensive front have more of an impact.

Maybe upon rewatching the game and breaking down the tape, we see some positives from this group, but my instant reaction to what I saw on Friday night was that I still want to see more. There's a lot of season left, and plenty of time to improve, but thus far, it doesn't feel as if this group is living up to the high expectations we had before the year.

Jeremiah McClellan warmed up before this game as if it were business as usual, but once the team came out right before kickoff, he emerged from the locker room in street clothes with a boot on his left foot, using crutches to walk. After the game, Lanning wasn't able to offer much of an update, saying that they needed to do more testing before they knew the extent of the injury.

"Got tweaked in pregame; have to get an evaluation to see what exactly that looks like," Lanning said . "I don't know right at this moment."

The timing is certainly unfortunate, with Oregon going on the road to face the No. 12 USC Trojans next week in a game that could ultimately define both teams' seasons. While the Ducks have pass-catching options aside from McCLellan, losing him for any amount of time would ding this offense and potentially slow Oregon's momentum. We will wait to hear more from Lanning on his status Monday night during his weekly press conference.

articles.title: Falcons Week 2 X-factor: Feed Kyle Pitts and Drake London
articles.summary: Atlanta's offense can't afford to be one-dimensional against Carolina
articles.body:
Things are trending the wrong way for the Atlanta Falcons heading into their Week 2 matchup with the Carolina Panthers . For one thing, they have lost four of their last five games against their I-85 rivals. For another, their offense was about as putrid and one-dimensional as you'll ever see at this level.

In their Week 1 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers , the Falcons started Cooper Rush at quarterback with disappointing resulted. The veteran QB will get the start again with Michael Penix Jr. out and Tua Tagovailoa doubtful for Sunday's game.

The biggest issue with Rush is that he seemed completely uncomfortable throwing the ball past the line of scrimmage. That lead to Bijan Robinson getting the lion's share of targets, totaling 10 - twice as much as any other player and nearly half of the team's 21 pass attempts .

If the Falcons are going to upset the Panthers, they need to get their other star skill players involved. Top wide receiver Drake London was only targeted five times last week, catching two of them and totaling 29 yards. Meanwhile, star tight end Kyle Pitts had it even worse, only seeing one target all afternoon and finishing with zero catches.

Rush must make better use of Atlanta's other options in the passing game. Pitts and London should see at least 11-12 targets between the two of them if the Falcons are going to force the Panthers to account for anybody but Bijan Robinson.

It also wouldn't hurt to see what Zachariah Branch could do, either. The rookie receiver out of Georgia flashed as a returner last week but was not involved offensively, at all.

Whoever's in the backfield has to spread the ball around a lot better than Rush did in Pittsburgh, or Atlanta is headed for an 0-2 start to the season.
